outline.rationale: The user is a total beginner whose goal is to build and ship models, so the outline is deliberately practical and end-to-end, minimizing theory and math. Node 1 gives just enough conceptual grounding to be dangerous without academic depth. Node 2 gets them into a working environment immediately since hands-on practice is central. Nodes 3–6 follow the natural build workflow: data prep, training, evaluation, and iterative improvement — the core loop of practical model development, kept MECE by separating data work, fitting, judging, and fixing. Node 7 is a reference-style node covering the model landscape so they can choose appropriately, placed after the workflow since it's a menu rather than a step. Nodes 8–9 directly address the 'ship' goal — deployment and post-launch operations — which distinguishes this user from someone who only wants to explore ML. I excluded history-of-the-field, proofs, and research-level math per the confirmed understanding.
